s01.text: The expert is bored within a minute.
The beginner is lost by minute two.
And a parent, watching with their child, can't remove the one moment they didn't want.

s02.text: Every tool we have treats a video as one solid block.
You can add a quiz, generate a script, add captions, or plan a path around it.
But nothing reaches inside the frame.

s03.text: So what if a video wasn't a block — but a set of threads?
This is LOOM. Live, object-grounded, orchestrated media.

s04.text: SAM 3.1 finds and tracks every object on screen.
Speech is transcribed, and on-screen text is read.
All three are fused into one concept graph: this beaker, at fourteen seconds, while the narrator says 'combine slowly', under this equation.

s05.text: Then a team of specialist agents gets to work.
The Curator cuts the graph into short threads.
Pedagogy matches them to what this learner already knows.
The Personalizer assembles the cut, and Assessment writes the checks.
They speak the open Agent-to-Agent protocol — so a school's own agent can join the team.

s06.text: Before anything is shown, a Critic checks it.
If the cut fails, it goes around again — but only within a fixed budget, and then falls back to the last verified version.

s07.text: Now the viewer can tap anything in the frame.
The Animator writes a short Manim animation for that exact concept — and caches it for the next learner.
And when one object isn't right for a young viewer, the Guardian masks just that object.
The rest of the lesson keeps playing.

s08.text: Same threads. A different weave for every viewer.
The expert gets the ninety-second version. The beginner gets the full walkthrough, with explainers. The parent keeps the rest of the video.
And every session updates a mastery graph, so the next one starts in the right place.
